precepts.text: That which I do I allow not; for what I would, that do I not; but what I hate, that do I. The real spirit connected to God hates evil, and the conditioned self does it anyway. That duality is the daily fight. Christ said deny yourself: the you doing the denying is what God is dealing with, and the self is the composite of conditioning. Examine your behaviour and ask whether it is the real you or a response to conditioning.
precepts.point: I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations. Whatever the Lord ordained us to be, we will be, and he put talents in us. That is why the Bishop stresses organizing those talents; you cannot bring self-doubt around him. Get the doubt out and let the real you stay and be built up.

note.label: The Image of Dysfunction or the Image of God Which One Are You?

precepts.why:
The foundational question is: am I who I was created to be, or am I what I was conditioned to become? It is not a surface-level question; it is an identity question that deals with the real soul of man and woman. Everything about us, our patterns, our responses, our beliefs, our defenses, has been shaped by one of two forces: creation or conditioning. Creation speaks to design; conditioning speaks to experience. One is intentional, the other reactive. One reflects origin, the image God made; the other reflects adaptation, to slavery, to ghettos, to being taken advantage of, to being unclean, a gang member, a drug addict. That is not who we really are, and most people live somewhere in between without ever telling the two apart.

Paul shows that fight in Romans 7:15: “For that which I do I allow not: for what I would, that do I not; but what I hate, that do I.” What he ends up doing, the real him does not allow. What his spirit would do, the conditioned self will not follow. And what the real him hates, the righteous part connected to God that hates evil, he does anyway, acting from conditioning and not from what the Lord made him to be. “If then I do that which I would not, I consent unto the law that it is good.” That duality goes on with us every day.

Christ said you must deny yourself. The you that does the denying is the part God is dealing with; the self is the composite of the conditioning you were made into. So examine your own thoughts and behaviors and ask: why am I behaving like this? Is this the real me, or a response to what I have been conditioned to be?

Most of the time when we deal with our people, we are dealing with the mask, the representative, like the man holding up a sign in front of himself. The real soul is buried and scared, hiding under a tarp of trauma, lies, deceit and psychological hang-ups. The greatness buried under self-doubt has not surfaced yet. That is what is meant by the Negro being made in a lab: the real him has not stood up. We have to encourage that real spirit to come forward and be the image God made.

precepts.text: God created man in his own image, blessed them, and said be fruitful and multiply and have dominion. This is the original declaration about you specifically, the real soul of man and woman, not the whore, drug addict, or dealer they told you that you are. You were made in the image of God, not in the image of your dysfunction, your traumatic experiences, an unstable childhood, an abusive relationship, or an environment that never reflected your worth. Before conditioning, survival strategies, and the false self, there was an image, and it carries creativity, dominion, and fruitfulness as original attributes in your DNA. Regardless of what you went through, you can fix it; IUIC told everybody who said we could not to go to hell.
precepts.point: I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations. Whatever the Lord ordained us to be, we will be, and he put talents in us. That is why the Bishop stresses organizing those talents; you cannot bring self-doubt around him. Get the doubt out and let the real you stay and be built up.

note.label: The Image of Dysfunction or the Image of God Which One Are You?

precepts.why:
You were created with intention: not randomly formed, not accidentally designed, not undefined in purpose. You have a purpose; you just lost your way. “So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them. And God blessed them, and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it: and have dominion.” Replenish the earth means have babies.

This is the original declaration, not only about humanity in general but about you specifically, the real soul of man and woman. Not the whore, the drug addict, the drug dealer they told you that you are. The real you is about righteousness, and you cannot define yourself by the conditioning of how you have been made to look. Conditioning says, we want to make a slave out of him, out of her, and make them think that is what they innately are. That is the point of saying the Negro was created in a lab: the real him has not stood up yet, the real us has not even surfaced yet.

You were made in the image of God, not in the image of your dysfunction. Not the image of your traumatic experiences, even though we have been through all kinds of trauma. Not the image crafted by an unstable childhood, an abusive relationship, or an environment that never reflected your worth back to you. Where it was said that we are not his people, it shall be said that we are the sons and daughters of God. We are not what they say we are; we are what God said we are. Carry yourselves that way and teach it to your children, because this world will turn them upside down if you are not serious about it.

Before conditioning entered, before survival strategies developed, before the false self was built, there was an image, an original design, and that design carries attributes: the capacity for creativity, for dominion, the capacity to rule, and for fruitfulness, children and nationhood. These are not just aspirations, like a novel we read. They are original; they are in our DNA, placed in us before the world opened its lips to say anything. When people see what we build and say it must be a sellout, that is a dysfunctional mind that believes we can't do anything. Men and women, whatever you went through, you can fix it. In IUIC we told everyone who said we couldn't to go to hell, and we did what we had to do.

precepts.text: Against any of the children of Israel shall not a dog move his tongue, against man or beast, that ye may know the Lord doth put a difference between the Egyptians and Israel. Not even a dog may speak against you. You are the jewellery God wears around his neck, the apple of his eye; carry yourself like that even in captivity, because it is temporary. They say you do not talk like a slave because I am not one. Christ on the cross knew he could call down legions, and we are joint heirs; the world is terrified of us making that connection.
precepts.point: I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations. Whatever the Lord ordained us to be, we will be, and he put talents in us. That is why the Bishop stresses organizing those talents; you cannot bring self-doubt around him. Get the doubt out and let the real you stay and be built up.

note.label: The Image of Dysfunction or the Image of God Which One Are You?

precepts.why:
The attributes of the image were placed in us before the world had its say, and Exodus 11:7 shows how God guards his people: “But against any of the children of Israel shall not a dog move his tongue, against man or beast: that ye may know how that the Lord doth put a difference between the Egyptians and Israel.”

Are we the children of Israel? Then not a dog shall open its lips against us. No one can talk against us or anything that belongs to us. The Lord put a difference so that the world may know. We are his holy jewels, the jewellery God will wear around his neck, the apple of his eye. When they speak against us, they are speaking against his jewels and his people.

Carry yourselves like that, and never mind people who say you can't boast. Even in captivity: it is only temporary. We are not the finished product of what they did to us. A day is coming when this will be gone, and everything that ever spoke against our people will face judgment. They say, you don't talk like a slave. That is because we are not slaves.

Be like Christ. On the cross, he knew he could call down legions to wipe them out in the blink of an eye, because he already had the power, and he says we will be joint heirs with him. The world is scared to death that we will ever make that connection. They do not want us connected to that kind of power.

precepts.text: This people have I formed for myself; they shall shew forth my praise. Teach your children they are superior, because they are; the world shows them Superman and Batman and tells them they are criminals. Sons need fathers in the household who think like that.
precepts.point: I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations. Whatever the Lord ordained us to be, we will be, and he put talents in us. That is why the Bishop stresses organizing those talents; you cannot bring self-doubt around him. Get the doubt out and let the real you stay and be built up.

note.label: The Image of Dysfunction or the Image of God Which One Are You?

precepts.why:
“This people have I formed for myself; they shall shew forth my praise.” This people is the Israelites, Judah: God formed us for himself, to show forth his praise, and all the other nations will catch hell.

Put that in your spirit and put it in your children's spirit. Teach your children they are superior, because they are. The world tells us lies: it shows us Superman and Batman and all kinds of fools on TV and makes us think we are nothing but criminals. Then, when we say the reverse, they try the Jedi mind trick and make us think we are doing something wrong. That is why sons need fathers in the household who think this way, so they grow up in the right posture.

We were not formed for survival or to be a product of our environment. We were formed for a purpose that comes from outside our circumstances, connected to the nature and intent of the Most High who formed us. That is Jeremiah 1:5: “Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee; and before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee.” Before the sperm hit the egg, we already existed and were known by him, and he chose which spirit to send, this one rather than that one, for a purpose. “and I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations”: whatever the Lord ordained us to be, we will be. He made us the children of Israel and put talents in us. That is why those talents must be organized and not wasted. Don't bring self-doubt; get the doubt out and let the real you stay and be built up.

precepts.text: Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee; and before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee, and I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations. So how can the Lord know how we are all going to move? Because it is already ordained. As Jeremiah is running around as a little kid playing with other little kids, the Lord said, when you grow up you are going to be a mighty prophet in the earth. The same way, especially with these young men. If I could go back in time and be ten, eleven, twelve years old learning this truth. But the good thing is, learning it when you did is ordained of the Lord. Because if you were ten, eleven, twelve back in the day, you may not have withstood those trials that came to many brothers and sisters back then, when YouTube was not as big as it is now. They did not have every topic and every class online for you to go and watch a class and say, let me get my spirit right. That did not exist. So when I was ten or eleven and a trial came, would I have withstood? Only the Lord knows. The Lord said, I will call you when I need you.
precepts.point: It is like a director, a screenplay writer. They write the movie, and you show up as the actor. They give you the script and you read it and say, this is a good movie, who am I going to play? Oh, I am going to be the Black Panther. Somebody may be morally torn by playing Killmonger, but Killmonger is actually the good guy. My point is Michael B. Jordan agreed to that role. Chadwick Boseman agreed to that role. Everybody agreed to their role, and then the movie was made and we all watched it and we were cheering, Wakanda forever. The same way, the Lord sat in his council and everyone was given their roles, their tasks. He already knew who was who, who was ordained to be in this womb.

note.label: Stay in the Spirit

precepts.why:
“Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee; and before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee, and I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations.” How can the Lord know how we are all going to move? Because it is already ordained, from the council Ezra speaks of, when he prepared the world “which was not yet made” and “no man spake against me.”

Think about it. As Jeremiah is running around as a little kid playing with other little kids, the Lord says, when you grow up, you are going to be a mighty prophet in the earth.

The same way with these young men. If I could go back and be ten, eleven, twelve years old learning this truth! But learning it when you did is ordained of the Lord. If you were ten, eleven, twelve back in the day, you may not have withstood the trials that came to many brothers and sisters then, when YouTube was not as big as it is now. There was not every topic and every class online for you to watch and say, let me get my spirit right. When I was ten or eleven and a trial came, would I have withstood? Only the Lord knows. The Lord said, I will call you when I need you.

That is every single one of us. It is ordained by the Lord for you young ones to be here in 2026, when your parents can send you a class for the spirit you are dealing with, so you are able to abide in this time. Many fell out back then. You were known and set apart before you came out of the womb, called at the time the Lord chose.

precepts.text: He tried to run away from it and the Lord did not let him. Like most of us: we see the task at hand, but we have not been fortified to see how important the mission is. Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee: the Lord sent a search party for you; he knew since the womb what he created. I sanctified thee, and I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations. Then said I, Ah, Lord God, behold, I cannot speak, for I am a child: I do not know much, I am weak, I am nobody. Most of my brothers have that same weak spirit; shake it off. The little that you know, that you mastered Deuteronomy 28 and breaking down John 3:16, the Lord can use; now apply it and let the Lord do his work. Give the Lord something to work with. Say not, I am a child: stop making excuses. Thou shalt go to all that I shall send thee, and whatsoever I command thee thou shalt speak; we are bound by that. Be not afraid of their faces: the same thing we just read in Ezekiel; same task, same mission. For I am with thee to deliver thee: that power with us is unstoppable. Brothers, gird up your loins.
precepts.point: Then I said, I will not make mention of him, nor speak any more in his name: that is Jeremiah experiencing being dismayed at all the work he was set to. But his word was in mine heart as a burning fire shut up in my bones; I could not stay. That is the course we are setting: our faces hardened with the word of God.

note.label: Making Our Face Harder Than Their Face

precepts.why:
“Then I said, I will not make mention of him, nor speak any more in his name.” That is Jeremiah dismayed at all the work he was set to. Go back to chapter 1 and see: he tried to run away from it, and the Lord did not let him. Most of us are the same; we see the task at hand, but we have not been properly fortified to see how important the mission is.

“Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee”. The Lord sent a search party for you; he already knew since the womb what he created. “and before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee, and I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations.” He hired you to be a prophet.

“Then said I, Ah, Lord God! behold, I cannot speak: for I am a child.” Lord, this work is too mighty for me; I don't know too much, I'm weak, I ain't nobody. Most of my brothers have that same weak spirit. Shake it off. The little that you know, that you mastered Deuteronomy 28 and smashing John 3:16, the Lord can use; now apply it and let the Lord do his work. Give him something to work with.

“But the Lord said unto me, Say not, I am a child”: stop making excuses. “for thou shalt go to all that I shall send thee, and whatsoever I command thee thou shalt speak.” We have to speak it; we are bound by that. “Be not afraid of their faces”: the same thing read in Ezekiel, the same task, the same mission. “for I am with thee to deliver thee, saith the Lord.” That power with us is great, unstoppable. Brothers, gird up your loins, and sisters too.

That is why, when Jeremiah tried to hold back, “his word was in mine heart as a burning fire shut up in my bones, and I was weary with forbearing, and I could not stay.” That is the course we are setting: our faces hardened with the word of God. And do not think we get beamed up by chariots and skip Jacob's trouble; our forefathers went through the suffering and we have to go through it too. That is the ticket to the kingdom.

precepts.text: Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee; and before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee. Where did he know us? In the spirit, before our parents brought us forth. There is something in your spirit that God said, I need to fix you, so that when the time comes you come back to me and not to your pride.
precepts.point: The same must know it after death by pain. This is a God that will kill you and still have pain awaiting. So do not let anybody tell you the place of torment was made up by a church; these scriptures are in the book.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart Hath Deceived Thee!

precepts.why:
Ezra says every one that shall be saved, and shall escape by his works, by keeping the commandments, and by faith in what is written, “Shall be preserved from the said perils, and shall see my salvation in my land, and within my borders: for I have sanctified them for me from the beginning.” That is when the kingdom is set up. And why does he say he sanctified them from the beginning? Jeremiah shows it.

“Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee; and before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee.” Where did he know us? In spirit. This is a physical domain, but he knew us in the spirit world, in another dimension. He did something to our spirit before our parents had relations to bring us forth. You are here because of a conversation God had with you before you even came into this world.

So you people are here because God cares about you. You are not here by accident. There is something in your spirit that God said, I need to fix you, so that when the time comes to destroy the earth, you come back to me and are not in your pride.

The third of Israelites were sanctified from the beginning, from the foundation of the earth. He said, these spirits I am going to love, and these spirits I am going to reject and destroy. God is good all the time to the people that keep his commandments. To you people breaking God’s laws, he is not good. So do not listen to anybody saying God is good all the time; that is not scriptural.

That is why the rest of the chapter is so hard: those who abused his ways, loathed his law while they had liberty and despised the place of repentance “must know it after death by pain.” The sanctified are preserved; the proud are not.

precepts.text: Is it time for you to dwell in your ceiled houses, and the house of the Lord lie waste? Now is not the time to build your own house first.
precepts.point: I have put my words in thy mouth; I have set thee over the nations and over the kingdoms, to root out, pull down, destroy and throw down, to build and to plant. Shake off the low self-esteem: the Black man has the strength to build brothers and sisters and to prophesy the destruction of these nations.

note.label: A Soul Without Purpose

precepts.why:
The Lord told Jeremiah, “Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee; and before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee, and I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations.” God sent Jeremiah with a purpose. But Jeremiah felt he was too young, that it was not the time: “Ah, Lord God! behold, I cannot speak: for I am a child.”

Some of us think the same way, that now is not the time. That is what Haggai answered: is it time for you to dwell in your ceiled houses, and the house of the Lord lie waste? Now is not the time to build your own house first. What about the house of the Lord?

The Lord did not accept Jeremiah's excuse: “Say not, I am a child: for thou shalt go to all that I shall send thee, and whatsoever I command thee thou shalt speak.” That is a commandment. Jeremiah did not have a choice; it was his from birth. It is the same for you and me: we were ordained from birth to do this work. God knows who you are and did not make a mistake calling you in here. Whatever weakness is in you is no coincidence, and neither is the seat you sit in. Ask yourself why you are here and not dead in the world.

So do not doubt yourself, and do not let Satan take the prize from you. Maybe it feels like too much work; just do it. Put the Lord's house before your own, and speak what we are commanded: Christ is a black man, sent to the twelve tribes of the house of Israel.

precepts.text: Set over nations to root out, pull down and throw down — and to build and to plant. Breaking down the spirit a man carries is part of it, but the building has to come behind it, and that authority must be wielded justly.
precepts.point: She goes quiet because she does not want to deal with it, and you call that effective while you are breaking her spirit. Leaders build; they do not only break.

note.label: To Whom Much Is Given: The Burden and Beauty of Godly Leadership

precepts.text: Jeremiah son of Hilkiah prophesied in the days of Josiah through Zedekiah, showing he was a prophet during this very time of reform.
precepts.point: Topheth was the place where the people sacrificed their children, and it had to be defiled because Israel would not stop the evil on its own.

note.label: 2 Kings 23: Josiah Reads the Law and Cleanses the Land

precepts.why:
“The words of Jeremiah the son of Hilkiah, of the priests that were in Anathoth in the land of Benjamin: To whom the word of the Lord came in the days of Josiah the son of Amon king of Judah, in the thirteenth year of his reign.” It came also in the days of Jehoiakim, “unto the end of the eleventh year of Zedekiah the son of Josiah king of Judah, unto the carrying away of Jerusalem captive in the fifth month.”

Jeremiah was a prophet during this very time of reform. What he says about Topheth speaks to the same place Josiah defiled.

precepts.text: Set over the nations to root out, pull down, destroy, throw down, build up, and plant the seeds of God's word in his people.
precepts.point: Receive the law from his mouth and lay up his words in your heart. If you return to the Almighty you shall be built up and put away iniquity far from your tabernacle. This was our job, to build up our people.

note.label: Job 22: Acquaint Now Thyself With Him

precepts.why:
“If thou return to the Almighty, thou shalt be built up”. Jeremiah was told, “See, I have this day set thee over the nations and over the kingdoms, to root out, and to pull down, and to destroy, and to throw down, to build, and to plant.”

That was our job: to build up our people. Set over the nations to root out, pull down, destroy and throw down, and then to build up and plant the seeds of God's word in his people. Returning to the Almighty is how a people is built up and puts iniquity far from its tabernacles.

precepts.text: The Most High knew us and formed us in the belly before we came forth.
precepts.point: That He made us and not we ourselves goes with the Most High forming us in the belly and knowing us before we were born.

note.label: Psalm 100: Make a Joyful Noise Unto the Lord

precepts.why:
“Know ye that the Lord he is God: it is he that hath made us, and not we ourselves; we are his people, and the sheep of his pasture.” That he made us and not we ourselves goes with the Most High forming us in the belly and knowing us before we were born.

He said it to Jeremiah: “Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee; and before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee, and I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations.” The Most High knew us and formed us in the belly before we came forth. We did not make ourselves; he formed us, and he knew us before the womb.

That is why we are his people and the sheep of his pasture, and why all lands are to serve him with gladness and come before his presence with singing.

precepts.text: The Most High sets His prophet over the nations to root out, pull down, and destroy, which is why Ezekiel had to prophesy Tyrus's total ruin to her face.
precepts.point: His horses shall cover her with dust and tread down her streets; he shall slay her people, spoil her riches, prey on her merchandise, break her walls, destroy her pleasant houses, and lay her stones, timber, and dust in the midst of the water. He will cause the noise of her songs to cease and make her like the top of a rock, a place to spread nets, built no more.

note.label: Ezekiel 26: The Fall of Tyrus

precepts.why:
The Most High told Jeremiah, “See, I have this day set thee over the nations and over the kingdoms, to root out, and to pull down, and to destroy, and to throw down, to build, and to plant.” That is what a prophet is set over the nations to do, and that is why Ezekiel had to prophesy Tyrus's total ruin to her face.

Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, “a king of kings, from the north”, comes with horses, chariots, horsemen and much people. Babylon serves as the Most High's sword against the nations that thought our downfall was their gain. He slays her daughters in the field, makes a fort and casts a mount against her, sets engines of war against her walls and breaks down her towers with his axes. The dust of his horses covers her, her walls shake at the noise of the horsemen and the wheels and the chariots, and he treads down all her streets.

They spoil her riches, prey on her merchandise, break down her walls, destroy her pleasant houses, and lay her stones, timber and dust “in the midst of the water”. The noise of her songs ceases, and she is made “like the top of a rock”, “a place to spread nets upon”, built no more. Rooted out, pulled down, destroyed, thrown down: “for I the Lord have spoken it”.

precepts.text: Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee, and ordained thee a prophet unto the nations; the spirit was known before conception.
precepts.point: All who heard were amazed, asking if this is not the same man who destroyed those who called on Christ's name. But Saul increased the more in strength and confounded the Jews at Damascus, proving that this is very Christ. He already knew the scriptures under Gamaliel; when Christ was revealed, everything started to make sense and he took it to another level.

note.label: Acts 9: A Chosen Vessel

precepts.why:
“Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee; and before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee, and I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations.” The spirit was known before conception. Jeremiah was sanctified and ordained a prophet before he came out of the womb, and Paul says the same of himself, separated from his mother's womb.

So the man who confounded the Jews at Damascus, proving that this is very Christ, was set apart for it before he was formed. What he learned under Gamaliel came alive when Christ was revealed.

precepts.point: When Paul says he conferred not with flesh and blood, he means no man taught him the doctrine or the gospel; Christ revealed it directly.

note.label: Galatians 1: Paul's Apostleship and the True Gospel

precepts.why:
God “separated me from my mother’s womb, and called me by his grace.” Paul was always ordained from his mother's womb, even though he was persecuting and killing the church, chasing them from city to city, locking them in jail. It was already ordained for him to fulfill his role.

Jeremiah says the same thing: “Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee; and before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee, and I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations.” Many of us, before we came from our mother's womb, the Most High separated us to be prophets.

note.label: Soul Searchers Looking for a Purpose

precepts.why:
That’s why the Lord judges our people: because of the innocent blood on our hands. “These six things doth the Lord hate: yea, seven are an abomination unto him: A proud look, a lying tongue, and hands that shed innocent blood.”

That child is innocent. That child ain’t came on the earth yet, but you took that child before it ever made it. Out of those 900,000, a large majority are Black and Hispanic, guaranteed, because they push the option of abortion harder in our communities. That’s in the Bible: hands that shed innocent blood.

note.label: Soul Searchers Looking for a Purpose

precepts.why:
Remember the Lord said he had a purpose for Jeremiah. “And now, brother, behold what glory; and see the people that come from the east: Unto whom I will give for leaders, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob”, and on through the prophets, Amos and Joel, Jonas, Nahum, Zachary and Malachy, “which is called also an angel of the Lord.”

So Abraham is back on the earth today. Abraham came back on this earth through the sperm of a man in captivity. These men, the fathers and the prophets, are going to be the leaders of the people that come from the east, the same way the Lord had already ordained Jeremiah before he was formed in the belly.

note.label: Soul Searchers Looking for a Purpose

precepts.why:
“For thy help will I send my servants”: the Lord said he is going to send Isaiah, and he is going to send Jeremiah, “after whose counsel I have sanctified and prepared for thee twelve trees laden with divers fruits.”

The Lord told Jeremiah, I sanctified thee a prophet. That means Jeremiah wasn’t just sanctified as a prophet when he lived as Jeremiah; he was sanctified as a prophet in today’s time, as he lives today. So you don’t know which one of these kids may be Jeremiah, but you going to go to the clinic and kill that baby. You don’t know what you doing.

And it’s not only the sisters: there are men that contribute to abortion too, that leave money on the nightstand and say go take care of that. There are wicked, no good men out there that kill babies too, so we ain’t just blaming the sisters. But we go so hard on the sisters because y’all are the ones that end up with the child, and you go through a lot with that child.

note.label: Soul Searchers Looking for a Purpose

precepts.why:
Jeremiah is back on the earth, but Jeremiah ain’t going to know he’s Jeremiah until a certain point in his life when he gets woken up, and even when he wakes up he’s still not going to know that he is the prophet Jeremiah.

“And thou, even thyself, shalt discontinue from thine heritage that I gave thee”: he is talking to Jeremiah, telling him that in the future he is going to discontinue from his heritage. “And I will cause thee to serve thine enemies in the land which thou knowest not”: he told Jeremiah he would go through slavery and be oppressed. “For ye have kindled a fire in mine anger, which shall burn for ever.”

So Jeremiah is back on the earth today, going through trials and tribulations and systemic oppression; he could have been incarcerated; he may not even have woken up yet, and right now he is possibly going through pure hell. What if he gives up and gives in to drugs, goes out and starts knocking brothers and sisters off, killing and robbing people, and completely wastes his purpose and his existence? He can’t do it. The Bible prophesied that he is going to be back on the earth in these last days teaching.

And you may be Jeremiah. Why you thinking about giving up, doing drugs, committing adultery? Don’t waste your purpose. Your purpose is not to be here to fulfill the lust of your flesh; your purpose is to be here to fulfill God’s will for you.

note.label: SABBATH NOON CLASS: History Repeats Itself - Message From Jeremiah

precepts.why:
The one king Jeremiah 1 does not mention is Jehoahaz: “Jehoahaz was twenty and three years old when he began to reign; and he reigned three months in Jerusalem.” “And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, according to all that his fathers had done.”

“And Pharaoh–nechoh put him in bands at Riblah in the land of Hamath, that he might not reign in Jerusalem; and put the land to a tribute of an hundred talents of silver”: the Egyptians were taxing Israel.

“And Pharaoh–nechoh made Eliakim the son of Josiah king in the room of Josiah his father, and turned his name to Jehoiakim.” This is the history of how Jehoiakim was made king. He was placed as king by the Egyptian pharaoh, set up as a vassal king, meaning ‘you’re gonna do whatever I tell you’: a puppet. It is like today, when America goes to different countries and sets up puppet rulers who are not really for the people; they are there on behalf of American policies, and that is all they are there for. It was the same thing with Jehoiakim: Pharaoh Necho set him up as a vassal king, “and took Jehoahaz away: and he came to Egypt, and died there.”

note.label: | Explaining Dark Sentences | Part 3

precepts.why: No man spake against God when he prepared the world, because everyone was already there in the spirit. “Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee; and before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee, and I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations.” Jeremiah was chosen to be a prophet in the spiritual realm before he was ever born. So it was with all of us: in the spiritual world every man, woman, boy and girl was there, and each was given the part to play, Israel, Moab, Ham, Esau, Ammon, and everybody obeyed.

note.label: Must Be Hated To Be Heard! The Price Of Speaking Truth To Modern Day Christians

precepts.why: “Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee.” God knew us before he formed us; we were chosen. “And before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee, and I ordained thee a prophet.” None of us is here by chance. It is ordained of God that in our time we would be woken up to who we are in the truth. Now that we know it, we have to get ourselves right and go out and find the people and bid them to this wedding. That is why we are on the corners and why we travel the world: to do the work God called us to do. We were ordained to be prophets.

note.label: Rise Of An Unseen Government

precepts.why:
That’s why the Lord said: “See, I have this day set thee over the nations”. He told Jeremiah what he said to all the prophets, all of us: I have set you over the nations. What does that mean? You are an ambassador.

“And over the kingdoms, to root out, and to pull down, and to destroy, and to throw down, to build, and to plant.” That is our job as ambassadors for Christ. We are official diplomats.

note.label: A FIRE SHUT UP IN MY BONES : THE WORK THE ZEAL THE FIRE

precepts.why:
Purpose is the reason for which something exists or is done, and Jeremiah knew his. “Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee”: God knew his soul and his spirit. “And before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee, and I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations.”

That was his purpose, and it stayed with him through everything he went through. To realize you have been called to something higher is what turns weariness into praise. Until you have graduated to purpose in this, you are just spending your time here, deciding by emotion and rationalizing after the fact.

Jeremiah went through all of it and realized there is something inside him that will never stop, and if it means he dies doing it, so be it. Purpose conquers weariness. We are going to get the reproach, but face it head on with zeal, trusting that the Most High is always faithful to his laborers.

note.label: PAUL THE PROPHET AND IDOL WORSHIP

precepts.why:
“Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee”: he knew Paul too, and that is what Paul just said. “Before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee”: I chose you. “And I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations.”

Just as Jeremiah was sanctified before he came out of the womb, Paul was separated “from my mother’s womb” and called by God’s grace: chosen to be a prophet. It is the same exact thing, being said by Paul. The Lord chose him before he was formed, despite what he did before Christ met him.

note.label: BOLD WITNESSES FOR THE KINGDOM

precepts.why:
Some think they have a choice, so Jeremiah 1. The words of Jeremiah came “in the days of Josiah the son of Amon king of Judah, in the thirteenth year of his reign”, on to Jehoiakim and Zedekiah, “unto the carrying away of Jerusalem captive in the fifth month.”

Then the word of the Lord came: “Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee”. Before I formed thee means before your mother was even pregnant, before you were in your mother’s womb, God knew you. “And before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee”: before your mother gave birth, God sanctified you. “And I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations.”

A leader’s, a prophet’s destiny is chosen for him. Your destiny was chosen for you; you cannot choose your own destiny. God ordained you a prophet. That is why, whether our people will hear or whether they will forbear, we have no choice but to go and tell them, Thus saith the Lord God.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 3 A Message to The 7 Churches

precepts.why: Him that overcometh will I make a pillar in the temple of my God: he that overcometh will I make a leader in the temple of my God. That is what he said to Jeremiah in his spirit, and what he said to Jeremiah goes to what he said right here, because it didn't come to pass during the time of Jeremiah. “For, behold, I have made thee this day a defenced city, and an iron pillar,” See that: he made Jeremiah an iron pillar, meaning a leader, a prophet. “and brasen walls against the whole land, against the kings of Judah, against the princes thereof, against the priests thereof, and against the people of the land.”

note.label: Give Diligence

How dare you let somebody take you off it playing in your sins, lusts, doubts, and fears.

note.label: A Soul Without Purpose

points: Now we know we dealing with Jeremiah. It says the sense of having been called even before his birth.
Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee: so the Lord said, before I formed thee in the belly, I knew thee. So the scholars had some sense. They knew what the scripture was saying.
To be a prophet. That's our calling, brothers and sisters. We ought to be prophets of the most high God.
He's called to be a prophet, as we just read, right?

This is according to the author here. Jeremiah's disposition was shy and shrinking. So it wasn't like he was a big mighty tall, like a massive individual. It says his outer appearance was shy and shrinking. So that's a testament to you and I. We might think, especially the brothers in the diaspora, like you're not as big, you don't have that courageous strong spirit that we should pray and ask the Lord for, you thinking you're not nobody. But you are somebody, believe it or not. You be thinking, you're reading the Bible, you see certain prophets, you thinking that they were so mighty and tall and massive. No, they were just like you and I.

A lot of us today, a lot of us got called, we were young when we came in this truth. Although Lord sanctified him in the womb, but he didn't start his ministry till when he was 20 or 25. Just like Christ. Christ didn't start teaching till he was 30, taught for 3 years.

Why this is so heavy: because a lot of time when we read the book, we never place ourselves in the context. We are the prophets of the most high God. We are Jeremiah, Ezekiel, Isaiah, Micah, Amos. We are the prophets. So we got to place ourselves there. That's how we going to strengthen our spirit, when we don't try to separate ourselves from our records.
He served his race and God. So even the scholars knew he ain't go to other nations. This is when he went to the 12 tribes of Israel.
So when Jeremiah came to yield his spirit to the Lord to serve and go teach, the surrender was absolute. Meaning he had no doubt. He was 10 toes down. That's a testament for you and I.

You see that? His life was completely consecrated to his divine task, to our calling. So that's a example for you and I. We have to take this truth to another level. We got to understand that this is our profession, this is our calling. This is not a hobby. We know what our hobby is, that 9-5 you and I have today in this captivity. That's a hobby. But our true purpose in existence is to serve the Lord, keeping the commandments and the faith in Christ, and go raise up the 12 tribes of Israel. That's our lot, that's our calling.

The same thing said to Jeremiah is what is happening today: the brothers and sisters waking up were formed in the belly and known from the beginning, raised up to prophesy against the nations.

The charge is idolatry, the very thing the rest of the reading opens up in detail.

note.label: Jeremiah 1: The Prophet Ordained unto the Nations

points: He is made a defenced city, an iron pillar, and brasen walls against the whole land; they shall fight but not prevail, for none can prevail against the word of the Most High going out through the prophets.

note.label: Jeremiah 1: The Prophet Ordained unto the Nations

points: Let’s talk about purpose. “Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee.” You all know what takes place: the sperm cell reaches the egg and activates it, the child is conceived and grows in the woman’s womb, and after nine months the body, the brain, the heart and the organs are fully developed and the baby comes. But before that even happened, while that spirit was in the heavens and the Lord sent that spirit through the father, the Lord already knew him. It was a decision made in heaven for you to be here.

Then you come down here and do drugs, kill yourself, let depression and anxiety overtake you, but that’s not what you was created for. A man carries millions upon millions of sperm cells every single day, but the Lord found it fit to make sure you were the one that reached the egg first. That’s not something to play with.

“And before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee”: before you came out of the womb he had already sanctified you. “And I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations.” When that sperm cell was on its way to the egg, the Lord said this one right here is going to be a prophet, and he ordained it while the mother was walking around six, seven, eight months pregnant, going through the morning sickness and the pain. The Lord was helping her through it, saying you about to bring forth a prophet.

That’s what the Lord said to Zacharias about John the Baptist, what he told Jeremiah right here, and what he told Mary about Christ. These men he is bringing back on this earth have a purpose, and it’s not just them. All of us have a purpose.

People out here struggling don’t understand they got a purpose. They built a box for safely abandoning newborn babies: you place the infant inside, take the orange bag of resources, shut the door and walk away, and it locks; your baby may be crying in there and you can’t get the baby out until the police show up, and they might take you to jail for abandoning the child. The white man is the devil; he going to give you every opportunity to break God’s commandments. They say the baby is only in there a minute and twenty-some seconds, but how many things can happen to make that baby suffocate in there? These folks hate us. They know we got a purpose, and as many of us as they can control and destroy, they’re going to do it.

The CDC counted 625,000 abortions in 2021 in the states it had data for, and the Guttmacher Institute’s count for 2020 was higher still: in one year almost a million babies were aborted, and less than 1% of those are from rape, though they always try to say that. Economic factors, social economic status, children out here having sex that shouldn’t be having sex and getting pregnant: nonetheless it’s wicked as hell. You don’t know that child’s purpose, what the Lord had for that child, and you eliminated that spirit from coming on this earth.

note.label: Soul Searchers Looking for a Purpose

points: “See, I have this day set thee over the nations and over the kingdoms”. God set the men, prophets, and leaders over the nations. “to root out”. Root out the evil and lies. “and to pull down”. Pull down the evil and lies. “and to destroy”. Destroy the evil and lies. “and to throw down”. Throw down the evil and lies. “to build, and to plant.” After tearing down the lies, our job is to build.

That's what we do in IUIC, in the streets and in this building. Our programs build brothers up to go into the streets and wake our people up. Before coming into the truth, I was a little boy in a man's body. The scriptures made me a man. I'd been in Christian churches all my life and never learned these things. Take care of your wife, children, and household. Get a job. You can't hold rank without a job. Take care of yourself and be a family man. That's spiritual uprising.

note.label: Spiritual Uprising: When God Shakes a Nation

points: “The words of Jeremiah the son of Hilkiah, of the priests that were in Anathoth in the land of Benjamin.” This gives Jeremiah’s tribe. Jeremiah was a Levite, of the priests: the Haitians. This is his people.

Jeremiah prophesied as Babylon was rising. Nineveh, the capital of Assyria, was completely destroyed in Jeremiah’s time, by the Babylonians allied with the Medes, and Babylon was getting power. Nineveh was the greatest city in the world at that time, the way America is the greatest and most powerful country in the world in our time, with 800 military bases throughout the world and 37% of its finances spent on weapons and war, when other countries spend 11% or 9%. That is all they are about, weapons and war: that is Esau’s blessing, to be blessed with the art of war and conquering.

note.label: SABBATH NOON CLASS: History Repeats Itself - Message From Jeremiah

points: “To whom the word of the Lord came in the days of Josiah the son of Amon king of Judah, in the thirteenth year of his reign.” Jeremiah was during the time of King Josiah.

At the battle of Carchemish, Assyria joined with Egypt to fight against Babylon, and they lost, because God prophesied that Babylon would be a world empire. Josiah tried to get involved and fight the Egyptian pharaoh Necho, and Necho told him his fight was not against him: God had sent him to fight against the king of Babylon. Josiah did not listen, and Josiah got killed.

note.label: SABBATH NOON CLASS: History Repeats Itself - Message From Jeremiah

points: “It came also in the days of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah king of Judah, unto the end of the eleventh year of Zedekiah the son of Josiah king of Judah.” Jeremiah was during the time of King Jehoiakim and also during the time of King Zedekiah, “unto the carrying away of Jerusalem captive in the fifth month.”
So the kings during Jeremiah’s ministry were Josiah, Jehoahaz, Jehoiakim and Zedekiah. Jehoahaz is the one king this chapter does not mention, because he was only king for three months.

note.label: SABBATH NOON CLASS: History Repeats Itself - Message From Jeremiah

points: On the reservation, the Gadites are drowning in the same thing: the brother who hopes the tidal wave comes back and brings some more beer is saying, let me get high so I can disconnect from this ugly reality; let me waste myself in this bottle. All the tribes face the same negro mind. God did not put him here to do that, and the Most High did not cause us to be born to end up like this.

The Lord said that before he formed you in the belly he knew you. That means our spirits existed with the Lord before he put your spirit into that sperm and egg to cause you to be born into this earth. Decisions were made in the heavens: I want you here rather than him, rather than her, at this time. There is a reason for that decision, which means you have a purpose.

Then we get here and our lives are wasted, to the point where the brother asked whether it matters if he lives or dies had to think about it. Is my life even worth living? You damn right it is: God made it and saw fit to have you born. But if you are disconnected from where you really belong, you will not see that; you will devalue yourself everywhere you go and let anything run over you, as if you are not even worth being heard. That is why our stories have to be told, turned all the way up, so our people can resonate with them. It is cathartic.
